A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RSPO and retain matching methods and core experiments. All pages, including appendices, equations, figures and tables, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RSPO benchmark results, regularization ablations, response-diversity measurements and synthetic experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds ArmoRM evaluations, PairRM comparisons and supplementary experimental results.

M1.justification: The RSPO loss, preference-based update direction, constant baseline, self-play procedure and divergence estimators remain unchanged. The additional Nash-MD representation expands the theoretical discussion without changing the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover UltraFeedback instruction prompts, AlpacaEval, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench and the same two synthetic scenarios. The new UltraFeedback validation evaluations introduce scoring procedures within retained instruction-response coverage, rather than a new task or dataset family.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 expands the AlpacaEval model comparison with GPT-4 Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, GPT-4 0314 and Mistral Medium. GPT-4 0613 and Llama 3 70B already appeared in v1 Figure 1. The core SPPO, Snorkel, SimPO and iterative DPO comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations use ArmoRM overall and attribute scores and PairRM head-to-head judgments on the UltraFeedback validation set. Table 7 also evaluates combined regularization with forward coefficient 0.01 and reverse coefficient 0.5. Existing training and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a mixture-weight sensitivity comparison in Table 7 and fuller iteration-wise evidence about SPPO over-optimization in Table 8. Table 4 adds a response-quality breakdown. The existing individual-regularizer sweeps, diversity analysis and synthetic examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experiments. The new statement about over 120 fine-tuned models does not specify repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The headline RSPO scores remain 35.44% AlpacaEval LCWR, 22.9 Arena-Hard and 7.75 MT-Bench. v2 substantially expands results with ArmoRM attribute scores, additional model and mixture comparisons, fuller SPPO trajectories, and PairRM win rates of 0.55, 0.57 and 0.50 against Snorkel, SPPO and SimPO. Combined RSPO's ArmoRM overall score exceeds SPPO's, but its honesty and helpfulness scores are lower.

T1.justification: v2 adds a Nash-MD equivalence derivation with explicit reverse-KL regularization in Equations (17)-(25), and explicitly discusses entropy-relative convexity and regularizer eligibility. Most existing convergence and gradient proofs remain. The added Equation (20) contains an unjustified zero-expectation step.

C1.justification: The framework, convergence, complementary KL effects and headline benchmark-improvement claims remain. The abstract, introduction and conclusion extend the claimed benefits to additional response-quality attributes, including instruction following, truthfulness and helpfulness.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial mechanism explanations involving reverse-KL mode seeking, forward-KL mass averaging, reference-policy multimodality and clipping-related diversity effects. Appendices A and E explicitly discuss forward KL's theoretical limitation and restricted model scale. Some new interpretations overreach: Section 4.3 claims reverse KL improves truthfulness despite lower scores than SPPO in Table 4.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly discloses eight A100 80GB GPUs for training and one for evaluation; v2 also states the study covers over 120 fine-tuned models. Table 6 consolidates regularization coefficients already supplied in v1. Divergence implementations and clipping thresholds remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to f-DPO, Ye et al.'s general-preference work and ArmoRM, while removing the Haarnoja and Malkin references. It sharpens positioning against offline divergence-based alignment and contrastive DNO/INPO objectives. Much earlier related-work coverage survives in Appendix B.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the method and experimental narrative are rewritten. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5 and Appendix B; implementation explanations move earlier, and some main-text derivations move into the appendices. The document's organization changes extensively.

P2.justification: The opening performance chart is replaced by a conceptual schematic. v1 Table 2 is split into v2 Tables 2 and 3; Tables 4, 6, 7 and 8 are added. Table wrapping, figure placement, captions and highlighting change throughout. Figures 2-6 retain their plotted data.

improvement.justification: Additional sensitivity and iteration results, hardware disclosure and explicit limitations improve transparency. However, new reliability problems accompany these gains: Section 4.3 overstates reverse-KL truthfulness results, Table 8 claims superiority over SimPO despite a 0.50 win rate, and Appendix A.2 Equation (20) unjustifiably cancels a response-dependent score-function term. With the core method and benchmark results unchanged, these competing benefits and harms prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
